planned_changes.change: Any reader failure in acquire (read_bytes or last_file raising an Exception, or the returned observation not establishing a current completed acquisition) is terminal for the call: record READ_FAILED, set stopped, perform one completion check of the original deadline (DEADLINE recorded if it raises an Exception or returns non-None; a BaseException propagates), then raise _Stop so no further acquisition or evaluation occurs. A later checker returning None can never resume acquisition. The stricter-cap conflict on an already completed cached entry stays a non-terminal READ_FAILED (no reader call).
planned_changes.cause_semantics: READ_FAILED (+DEADLINE when the completion check fails); HELD; no records

planned_changes.change: Store an attempt marker in the per-call cache BEFORE invoking read_bytes; any later use of a path whose attempt never completed raises READ_FAILED without another reader call or partial evidence. Completed entries keep the v2 coherent-cache behavior.

Assemble the complete candidate result (state.result) first; then, unless the state is already stopped, perform the final original-deadline check; on failure return a newly assembled HELD result with records and adapter3_inputs null and no acquisition; on success return the candidate unchanged.

Exactly one report() attempt per call on every path: _reader_unresolved marks the attempt before invoking report(); the normal path attempts it after evaluation, the fallback after _Stop/Exception, and an outer except BaseException handler attempts it only if not yet attempted, catches any secondary failure (any BaseException) into per-call state without replacing the primary, then re-raises the original object with a bare raise.
planned_changes.disclosed_limit: On the BaseException path no result is returned, so the retained secondary report failure is not externally observable; the caller-retained reader remains the authoritative report source (EXTERNAL_PREREQUISITES CALLER_RETAINS_GLOBAL_READER_REPORT_AND_OWNERSHIP).
